correctness.rationale: The graph is explicitly KG(5,2), with disjointness adjacency. The recurrence F_t(v,B)=sum_{w in N(v)∩B}F_t(w,B\{w}), base [v=t], counts all Hamiltonian paths by exhaustive first-step decomposition. It gives four paths between any nonadjacent endpoints, zero between adjacent endpoints, hence 120 paths. The natural S5 action has trivial stabilizer of the given base path: an orientation-preserving stabilizer fixes every 2-subset; an orientation-reversing stabilizer would have to fix 0, exchange 1/2 and preserve {3,4}, contradicting the required image of the second path vertex. Four explicit endpoint rotations of this base path give precisely alpha=(1 2 3 4), alpha^-1, beta=(1 4), gamma=(0 1)(3 4). Equivariance proves the Cayley identification. Alpha and beta generate S4 on 1..4; gamma combines with (3 4) to yield (0 1), so connectivity is proved analytically. The 120 complete Cayley distance/neighbor rows give sphere sizes 1,4,11,25,39,29,11 and exact diameter six, checked by the standalone first verifier. A separately written brute-force direct path-permutation enumerator constructs the path rotation graph without the Cayley certificate or generators and checks all 120 starts, 240 edges, and diameter-six profile. No infinite claim or sampling is used.

originality.rationale: The classical Pósa rotation is not new. The 2005 Oberdorf et al. preprint defines equivalent backbite moves and illustrates transition graphs of Hamiltonian walks on square grids. The 2026 Kazazi preprint (full text inspected) formalizes exactly the same Hamilton-path backbite reconfiguration graph, proves connectivity when a graph contains a spanning squared path, and constructs counterexamples; it does not discuss Petersen, and the Petersen cubic graph cannot contain the squared 10-vertex path (internal squared-path vertices have degree four). General Petersen automorphism group facts and the known 120 paths do not imply their rotation graph has the computed four right-Cayley generators or diameter six. Searches of published research records, primary texts, and external aliases found no prior Petersen-specific equivalent classification. Genuine priority risk remains for unindexed datasets and the 1993 Petersen monograph not inspected in full.
residual_risks: Holton–Sheehan 1993 Petersen monograph was not inspected in full; it could contain Hamilton-path reconfiguration data.
Historical or unindexed backbite/rotation transition tables may contain the same Cayley result; negative search is not a novelty proof.
The finite 120-row distance census is checked by two algorithms but not subject to independent third-party mathematical audit.

value.rationale: The exact natural state graph of all Hamiltonian paths under a single minimal path move is a motivated combinatorial reconfiguration object, important for reachability and local sampling of spanning paths. Identifying its entire geometry as a simply transitive S5 Cayley graph is a structural classification, not a parameter renaming or routine increment. Exact connectedness, four explicit group generators, and a sharp six-move worst-case distance answer a precise dynamical question for the canonical sparse non-Hamiltonian cubic graph. This yields a transparent low-degree connected example outside the known dense squared-path sufficient hypotheses. Complete certificate makes the exact six bound reusable. No general theorem or priority certification is falsely claimed.
